latest_news.title: Shaky Iran, Lebanon and Gaza ceasefires leave core disputes unresolved
latest_news.summary: AP reports no public Iranian concessions on nuclear, missile or proxy issues; Hormuz remains closed and planned weekend talks appeared to fall apart. Lebanon border fighting and Gaza strikes persist under nominal truces.

latest_news.title: UN: more than two dozen killed in Gaza; over 100 Israeli airspace violations over Lebanon
latest_news.summary: UN agencies and UNIFIL reported weekend Gaza deaths, damage near Al-Aqsa Hospital, and more than 100 Israeli violations of Lebanese airspace despite ceasefire arrangements.

latest_news.title: Chinese amphibious group and bombers surged to Scarborough Shoal drills
latest_news.summary: USNI adds force-composition detail to the Reuters/AP-confirmed 1 August joint Chinese air and naval combat drills around the disputed shoal; no armed clash was reported.

latest_news.headline: Oil remains sharply lower on deal hopes, but Hormuz reopening is still unverified
latest_news.summary: Reuters reported oil sliding by about $4 after Washington held off on a new strike in hopes of a deal. The 18:02 UTC local feed showed Brent at $83.71 and WTI at $80.30, still 24.2% and 25.9% above pre-conflict baselines. Oman-mediated route discussions continue, but neither a comprehensive U.S.-Iran channel nor sustained Hormuz throughput recovery is verified; no probability or signal changed.

latest_news.headline: Reuters: Iran pursues calibrated pressure through shipping and energy chokepoints
latest_news.summary: Reuters reports Tehran is using Hormuz, Red Sea threats and regional energy exposure to raise the cost of confrontation while avoiding a decisive full-scale expansion. Iran still denies current direct U.S. talks; Oman route discussions remain insufficient to reopen Hormuz. This reinforces existing active signals but does not justify raising the already extreme tracker score.

latest_news.headline: Russia adds Black Sea ship protection after sharp escalation in maritime attacks
latest_news.summary: Reuters says Russia formed a task force for alternative cargo routes and is adding Defence Ministry protection after reciprocal attacks on commercial vessels and agricultural export infrastructure intensified. The war tracker remains at its conventional-war ceiling, so no probability or canonical signal changed.

latest_news.headline: Russian naphtha tanker reroutes around Africa as Red Sea traffic thins
latest_news.summary: Reuters/LSEG tracking shows Sea Icon abandoned a Bab el-Mandeb transit and diverted around Africa; commodity-vessel traffic also fell to 18 on Sunday after the Houthi maritime embargo. The rerouting confirms persistent disruption already captured by the 100/imminent tracker; no new signal was added.

latest_news.headline: Iran denies current U.S. talks; Oman channel limited to temporary Hormuz route
latest_news.summary: Reuters reports Iran is not currently holding talks with the United States. Tehran says it is discussing a temporary safe route with Oman but that this would not be sufficient to reopen Hormuz while U.S. operations continue. This weakens near-term deal optimism without creating a new canonical signal or changing the already extreme 94/100 raw/coupled score.

latest_news.headline: Heavy federal-Tigrayan clash breaches Pretoria peace; fighting later halts
latest_news.summary: AFP, Al Jazeera and France 24 corroborated heavy fighting near Shererina in western Tigray on 1 Aug after months of force mobilization and peace-framework erosion. AFP local and security sources said the exchange ended later Saturday, but forces remain massed and the unresolved Sudan/Eritrea dimension leaves recurrence risk critical.

latest_news.headline: U.S.-Iran talks set for Monday as oil drops sharply on deal hopes
latest_news.summary: Reuters reports President Trump said negotiations would take place on 3 Aug with no deadline. Iran said Oman-mediated Strait-management talks were in their final stages but separated route negotiations from reopening. Brent fell more than 6% to about $82 in early trade; the local feed later showed $84.29, still 25.1% above its pre-conflict baseline.

latest_news.headline: Projectile disables laden LNG carrier in Strait of Hormuz as shipping talks advance
latest_news.summary: The Maritime Executive, citing maritime reporting, says an unknown projectile hit GasLog Shanghai near its engine room late 31 Jul, disabling the Qatar-loaded LNG carrier without casualties. A second vessel reported a near impact. Traffic remained reduced, but Oman-Iran shipping negotiations were reported close to an agreement; attribution is not independently settled.

latest_news.headline: Second straight day of Gaza strikes kills at least 18; Israeli minister says no halt deal
latest_news.summary: Reuters reports at least 18 Palestinians were killed on 2 Aug, the biggest daily toll in weeks. Energy Minister Eli Cohen said Israel had not agreed to halt attacks and could seek full control if Hamas does not disarm; mediators continue work on the implementation roadmap.

latest_news.headline: BBC Verify confirms large Russian military-vehicle shipment reached Mali
latest_news.summary: BBC Verify matched satellite imagery, ship tracking and verified Malian state-TV footage showing a large convoy of Russian-supplied trucks, armoured personnel carriers and light infantry vehicles in Bamako on 25 Jul. The delivery is direct external backing for Malian and Russian forces amid JNIM and Tuareg advances.

latest_news.headline: Ceuta border-surge death toll rises to 72 as most entrants return
latest_news.summary: Five more bodies were recovered, bringing the confirmed toll to 72. Reuters/Al Jazeera report more than 48,000 of roughly 60,000 entrants returned to Morocco within 48 hours and conditions improved markedly, while EU states sought coordinated border action.

latest_news.headline: U.S. European Command reportedly warns missile-defense ship capacity is stretched
latest_news.summary: The Washington Post, reported by Haaretz and other outlets, says the EUCOM commander warned that without another destroyer he may have to prioritize U.S. homeland defense over intercepting Iranian missiles aimed at Israel. The Pentagon and EUCOM did not comment; this is an allied-capacity warning, not a new combat signal.

dashboard_trackers.name: IRAN NUCLEAR
dashboard_trackers.notes: No current official reporting crossed a configured Iranian atomic-program threshold. Agency access uncertainty persists; direct Agency news and press endpoints were unavailable to the fallback collector, so official report indexes, UN material and reputable reporting were used. Raw/coupled risk holds 56/64

dashboard_trackers.name: IRAN WAR
dashboard_trackers.notes: Reuters reported on 3 Aug that Iran said it was not currently holding talks with the United States, contradicting Washington’s expectation of Monday negotiations. Tehran is discussing only a temporary safe route through Hormuz with Oman and says that would not reopen the Strait while U.S. operations continue. Raw/coupled risk holds 94/100: diplomacy remains active through Oman, but no comprehensive U.S.-Iran channel or reopening is verified

dashboard_trackers.name: ISRAEL-LEBANON
dashboard_trackers.notes: Ceasefire violations continue. Israel reported killing Hezbollah fighters on 2 Aug, while the cause of the blast that wounded five Lebanese soldiers remained contested: Lebanon initially blamed Israel and the IDF later attributed it to a Hezbollah device. Raw/coupled risk holds 95/100

dashboard_trackers.name: TURKEY-NATO
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h NATO, official and wire review found no direct Türkiye-alliance combat threshold or new missile/nuclear signal. Baseline risk holds at 5

dashboard_trackers.name: INDIA-PAKISTAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h wire and official review found no corroborated new India-Pakistan interstate combat threshold. A recycled low-quality headline about four Pakistani troops was traced to an old LoC incident and was not scored. Risk holds at 15

dashboard_trackers.name: PAKISTAN-AFGHANISTAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h regional, UN and wire review found no distinct new cross-border operational threshold. Existing diplomacy remains active and risk holds at 46

dashboard_trackers.name: RUSSIA-UKRAINE
dashboard_trackers.notes: Deep strikes and ballistic attacks continue at realized-war intensity, including reported attacks on oil, bomber and maritime targets. No separate nuclear or NATO-entry threshold was verified; conventional-war risk remains capped at 99

dashboard_trackers.name: RUSSIA-NATO
dashboard_trackers.notes: The 30 Jul Russian missile impact in Poland remains the key allied-territory event. No Article 4/5 invocation or direct NATO-Russia exchange was found; reported U.S. destroyer/interceptor strain affects allied capacity but is not itself a combat threshold. Raw/coupled risk holds 70/80

dashboard_trackers.name: CHINA-TAIWAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h Taiwan and allied-source review found no new blockade or invasion threshold beyond already-priced military pressure. Raw/coupled risk holds 24/28

dashboard_trackers.name: DPRK
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h KCNA, allied and wire review found no verified nuclear test or major missile-launch threshold. Risk holds at 18

dashboard_trackers.name: SUDAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: UN, CFR and major-source review found no de-escalatory break or fresh threshold beyond Sudan’s already extreme war baseline. Risk holds at 94

dashboard_trackers.name: ISRAEL PALESTINE
dashboard_trackers.notes: Reuters reported at least 18 Palestinians killed in a second straight day of Gaza strikes, the biggest daily toll in weeks, while an Israeli security-cabinet minister said there was no deal to halt attacks. The implementation roadmap remains active; risk stays near ceiling at 98

dashboard_trackers.name: SOUTH SUDAN ABYEI
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h UN and wire review found no distinct Abyei or South Sudan threshold change. Risk holds at 19

dashboard_trackers.name: EASTERN DRC
dashboard_trackers.notes: UN and regional review found no post-cutoff interstate or major-force threshold beyond continuing M23/armed-group conflict; a prison escape was not scored as regional escalation. Risk holds at 56

dashboard_trackers.name: YEMEN RED SEA
dashboard_trackers.notes: Houthi pressure on Saudi-linked shipping and attacks on tankers remain active. A Guardian planning report from Yemeni sources remains a watch item, but no launched al-Bayda operation was verified. Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb risk holds at 100

dashboard_trackers.name: MALI SAHEL
dashboard_trackers.notes: BBC Verify confirmed that a sanctioned Russian ship delivered a large shipment of armoured and military vehicles for Malian and Russian forces, with the convoy seen in Bamako on 25 Jul amid rebel advances. This is fresh corroboration of external backing; raw/coupled risk rises 39→43

dashboard_trackers.name: SOUTH CHINA SEA
dashboard_trackers.notes: Chinese naval, air and coast-guard drills around Scarborough Shoal remain the key recent military-pressure event. No collision, boarding or armed exchange was reported; risk holds at 35

dashboard_trackers.name: SOMALIA GULF OF ADEN
dashboard_trackers.notes: Maritime and regional-source review found no new piracy or shipping-disruption threshold in the past 24h. Risk holds at 28

dashboard_trackers.name: SOUTHERN THAILAND
dashboard_trackers.notes: Regional review found no distinct new attack cluster or deployment threshold. Older insurgency and peace-talk reporting did not justify a new signal; risk holds at 30

dashboard_trackers.name: KUWAIT IRAQ BORDER
dashboard_trackers.notes: Kuwait reported destroying multiple Iranian drones and damage from debris/strikes at northern critical facilities and Bubiyan Island, without casualties. The existing infrastructure_strike signal is reinforced; risk holds at 30 pending casualties, penetration or retaliation

dashboard_trackers.name: IRAQ INTERNAL CONFLICT
dashboard_trackers.notes: U.S.-Saudi strikes on Iran-aligned groups and militia retaliation threats remain the key escalation evidence. No distinct post-cutoff widening was verified; risk holds at 40

dashboard_trackers.name: KENYA SOMALIA BORDER
dashboard_trackers.notes: The 29 Jul al-Shabaab ambush that killed five Kenyan security officers remains the key event. No further verified cross-border step change was found; risk holds at 25

dashboard_trackers.name: EGYPT MEDITERRANEAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: The 29 Jul drone-caused fire on two gas vessels at Damietta remains the key spillover event. Port operations resumed and no new strike was verified; risk holds at 20

dashboard_trackers.name: SPAIN MOROCCO CEUTA
dashboard_trackers.notes: Reuters/Al Jazeera reported five more bodies, lifting the confirmed Ceuta death toll to 72. More than 48,000 entrants returned to Morocco and conditions improved markedly, so risk holds at 22/elevated with a falling trend

dashboard_trackers.name: ETHIOPIA TIGRAY
dashboard_trackers.notes: AFP, Al Jazeera and France 24 corroborated heavy federal-Tigrayan fighting near Shererina on 1 Aug after months of mobilization and TPLF claims that the Pretoria framework had collapsed. AFP sources said the exchange halted later that day; the pause limits the initial score to 32/critical, but opposing forces remain mobilized and regional spillover toward Sudan/Eritrea is unresolved

allied_positions.nato: No new Article 4/5 action or direct NATO-Russia exchange was found after the 30 July Russian missile impact in Poland; official NATO lanes and major-source review were checked.
allied_positions.gulf: The threatened fresh U.S. strike remains on hold, but Iran has not publicly accepted the proposed terms. No verified new Gulf energy strike or complete Hormuz closure/reopening threshold was found.
allied_positions.un_iaea: No new verified Iranian nuclear threshold was located. Direct IAEA news/press access returned HTTP 403, so official board-report indexes, UN material and reputable secondary reporting were checked instead; absence was not scored as calm.
allied_positions.israel_lebanon_gaza: Gaza implementation risk worsened: AP reports at least 17 killed and Israel raised serious concerns over the disarmament framework. In Lebanon, responsibility for the explosion that wounded five soldiers remained disputed; no settlement or distinct new strategic threshold was verified.
